rows.description: A student notices friends judging the same behaviour differently depending on who does it. Naming it gently, without accusing, helps them see the pattern in themselves.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague notices that people hire and promote those from their own college, region or community. Comfort with the familiar can look like merit and quietly shut others out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A mature adult checks their own assumptions, seeks out different views and speaks up when a group is mocked. They stay loyal to their own people without needing others to be lesser.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: When something goes wrong, a group of children agrees that one child did it. Pinning blame on a single, weaker child calms the group's own fear of being blamed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child becomes the default culprit in class or at home and starts to expect it. They may act out, withdraw or take on the label as a self-image.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A friend group under stress, such as exams or a conflict, starts blaming one member for everything. The blame relieves the group's tension while the target carries it alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager finds that friends who were warm suddenly blame and avoid them. They feel bewildered, betrayed and often ashamed, blaming themselves for a group's dynamics.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who sees a peer being blamed joins in lightly, out of fear of becoming the next target. The relief of being on the safe side hides how much it costs them inside.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, relief, trust

rows.subtype: Asking who really benefits from blame [Observer]
rows.description: A thoughtful peer notices that the group is unusually keen to blame one person and asks what the group is avoiding. Naming the pattern quietly can shift the mood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Standing up for the blamed person [Response]
rows.description: A peer states the facts calmly, asks for evidence and refuses to join. Even one person breaking the unanimity often stops a scapegoating spiral.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
